newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner profits up, sees firm 96 growth.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner profits up, sees firm 96 growth.

text.p: Dresdner Bank Thursday reported a 30 percent rise in nine-month profits, despite a surprising drop in trading income, and stuck to its forecast for a solid growth in full-year earnings.

Germany's second biggest commercial bank said its operating profit rose to 1.89 billion marks ($1.25 billion) in the period ended on Sept. 30, from 1.46 billion marks ($966 million) in the 1995 period.

The results were in line with analysts' forecasts but marked a slowdown from the 44 percent growth achieved at the half-year stage. Analysts expressed surprise at a 14.8 decline in trading profits for the bank's own account.
"The trading result was disappointing," said Dieter Hein, analyst at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.
But Dresdner said its year-end trading income should show a double-digit rise, once pending earnings were realised.

Dresdner also said its chief executive Juergen Sarrazin was expecting "clear double digit growth in (operating) earnings for the full year," stressing the bank's nine-month operating earnings already nearly matched its full earnings for 1995.
The bank's spokesman specified that the profit rise would be more than "just 10 or 15 percent."

Dresdner also announced plans to launch a direct banking unit in the second half of 1997, a long awaited move which follows a path already taken by its major rivals. It gave no precise details on the direct banking venture but said it would increase its use of technology and reduce its regular branch network in a bid to cut costs.

Dresdner also said it expected its commissions from the Deutsche Telekom issue, Germany's largest ever public offering which takes place in November, to be in the double-digit millions of marks in the fourth quarter.
Dresdner is one of the three global coordinators for the flotation.
